summary: Steel tower now on fire department grounds in Tobermory, Ontario; sources do not name its original site, and two accounts disagree on its state.

facts.status_note: Sources disagree: Firelookout.ca describes a standing tower; a Forest Rangers page says the old tower's remains sit on the site.

evidence.supports: Address in Tobermory, Municipality of Northern Bruce Peninsula, Bruce County
evidence.quote: 8, Nicholas Street, Tobermory, Municipality of Northern Bruce Peninsula, Bruce County, Southwestern Ontario, Ontario, N0H 2R0, Canada

evidence.supports: Stands behind Station 10 of the Northern Bruce Peninsula Emergency Services
evidence.quote: The Bruce County Fire Tower stands tall behind the Northern Bruce Peninsula Emergency Services, Station 10 Fire Department.

evidence.supports: Not its original home; has been there for many years
evidence.quote: Though not its original home the tower has been here for many years.

evidence.supports: Old tower's remains sit on fire department grounds in Tobermory
evidence.quote: The old Bruce County Tower's remains sit on the grounds of the Northern Bruce Peninsula Fire Dept. in Tobermory

evidence.supports: Page refers to a 2013 MNR decision, so it is undated but from about that time
evidence.quote: The Ontario MNR has decided, as of 2013, to remove many of these towers still standing.

notes_for_editor: Two accounts disagree on state: Firelookout.ca says the steel tower stands behind Station 10, while the undated Forest Rangers page says the old Bruce County tower's remains sit on the fire department grounds. Both put it in Tobermory, so the story reports the disagreement. Searches (one WebSearch, one websearch.py) found no original site, build date, staffing or fire record; Tobermory results were lighthouses and were not used. The Forest Rangers page is undated and refers to a 2013 MNR decision. The fandom page on the Northern Bruce Peninsula Fire Department returned 403 and was not used. No source gives an access level, so none is recorded.
